title: 山中问答
titleEn: Question and Answer in the Mountains
author: 李白
intro: Someone asks Li Bai why he lives up in the green mountains. He only smiles — and answers with a picture of peach blossoms drifting downstream into another world.
analysis: 这首诗用一问一答的形式写隐居山中的快乐。第一句是别人问：你为什么住在这青山里？第二句是回答——其实没有回答，只是笑笑，心里自在悠闲。为什么不回答？因为这种快乐说不清楚，说出来反而没意思了。第三四句用景物代替回答：桃花落在流水上，远远地漂走了，这里另有一片天地，不是人间。“桃花流水”让人想起陶渊明《桃花源记》里的世外桃源。诗人用“不答”来答，用画面代替道理，读者自己去体会，这就是中国诗常说的“言有尽而意无穷”——话说完了，意思还没完。语言轻松自然，像随口说出来一样。
analysisEn: The poem is a tiny conversation about living in the mountains. Line one is the question: why do you choose to live up in these green hills? Line two is the answer — or rather, no answer: the poet just smiles, his heart at ease. Why not explain? Because some kinds of happiness can’t be put into words; explaining would spoil them. So the last two lines answer with a picture instead: peach petals ride the stream far away into the distance; here is a different world, not the world of ordinary people. Peach blossoms on flowing water would remind any Chinese reader of Tao Yuanming’s “Peach Blossom Spring”, the story of a hidden paradise found by following petals upstream. Answering by not answering, and giving an image instead of a reason, leaves room for readers to feel it for themselves — a quality Chinese critics praised as “the words end, but the meaning goes on”. The tone is light and offhand, as if Li Bai tossed it off with a grin.
background: Li Bai (701–762) spent time as a young man living in the mountains near Anlu (in today’s Hubei), reading and studying Daoism. The poem is usually dated to those years; an alternative title is “Answering Ordinary People in the Mountains” (山中答俗人).
pronunciation: 栖 qī；窅然 yǎo rán（深远的样子）。机器朗读“窅”可能读错，已在朗读用字中换成同音的“杳”。
version: 采用通行文本。题目一作《山中答俗人》。异文：“窅然去”一作“杳然去”，意思相同。

lines.py: wèn yú hé yì qī bì shān
lines.lit: You ask me for what reason I perch in the green mountains;
lines.en: You ask me why I make my home among green hills;

lines.py: xiào ér bù dá xīn zì xián
lines.lit: I smile and do not answer; my heart is at ease by itself.
lines.en: I smile and say nothing; my heart is at peace.

lines.py: táo huā liú shuǐ yǎo rán qù
lines.lit: Peach blossoms and flowing water go off into the far distance;
lines.en: Peach petals float off on the stream, far out of sight —

lines.py: bié yǒu tiān dì fēi rén jiān
lines.lit: there is another heaven and earth, not the human world.
lines.en: this is another world, not the one where people live.

words.note: 古代第一人称，现代汉语说“我”。
书面语，现代汉语说“为什么”。
本义是鸟停在树上，现代汉语“栖息”“两栖动物”。
碧：青绿色，现代汉语“碧绿”“碧水蓝天”。
今天仍常用，形容不愿或不必回答。

words.en: far and deep, fading from sight
words.note: 书面语，同“杳然”，今天说“杳无音信”。
今天仍是常用成语，形容风景或境界特别引人入胜，如“别有洞天”。
现代汉语仍用，如“人间天堂”。

imagery.name: 山
imagery.zh: 碧山是诗人隐居的地方，远离世俗的清静之地。
imagery.en: The green mountains are the poet’s retreat, a quiet place far from worldly life.

imagery.name: 桃花
imagery.zh: 桃花随流水漂走，让人想起“世外桃源”，代表理想中的美好世界。
imagery.en: Peach petals drifting downstream recall the Peach Blossom Spring — an ideal, hidden paradise.

imagery.name: 水
imagery.zh: 流水把桃花带向远方，引人想象山中更深处的另一个世界。
imagery.en: The stream carries the petals away and draws the imagination deeper into the mountains, towards another world.

imagery.name: 天地
imagery.zh: “别有天地”说山中自成一个世界，和喧闹的人间完全不同。
imagery.en: “Another heaven and earth” — the mountains form a world of their own, utterly unlike the noisy human one.
